decisions.decision: One plan or several
decisions.ruling: Two plans. Plan 1 (this folder) removes the three packs and moves MCP ownership to the user. Plan 2 requires this folder: the generator researches without Context7, and the 142 passive Context7 hints (B124) are decided
decisions.rejected: One plan with everything; three plans, one per tool

decisions.decision: What plan 1 does with the generator, which still needs Context7
decisions.ruling: Reword the halt only. The generator keeps requiring Context7 until plan 2. When no Context7 server is reachable, it asks the user to install a Context7 MCP server themselves (user scope), names the official install page, and waits; it never installs one and never names a tools menu option
decisions.rejected: Change nothing (the halt then names a removed menu option); move the full rework into plan 1

decisions.decision: Who installs MCP servers
decisions.ruling: The user. User's words: 'I want the ownership of install mcp servers to move to user and not this plugin. Wherever the mcp servers are required, AI agent should simply ask the user to install them.' The pack key user_mcp_servers: is retired: no pack declares it, the generator emits none, the materializer writes none, and vwf-tools holds LSP servers only. The tier-3 consent keeps only its LSP part
decisions.rejected: Keep user_mcp_servers: for generated packs; a separate plan for the ownership move

decisions.decision: How a pack declares that it needs an MCP server
decisions.ruling: A '## MCP servers' section in the pack's conventions.md, beside the existing '## Claude plugins' section. One line per server: its name, what it is for, and its official install page. It is not handed to bootstrap. When a skill needs the server and it is not available, the agent asks the user to install it and waits. Doctor reports a declared server that is not available as drift, never blocking
decisions.rejected: Skill text only, with no structured declaration; a pack.yaml key such as required_mcp_servers:

decisions.decision: How a repo that pins context7, notion or claude-design moves off them
decisions.ruling: config_format 26. The /vwf:setup migration removes context7 and notion from addons: through the existing remove: path. It removes every MCP server key that vwf-tools holds (its .mcp.json-style server entries and claims for MCP keys), with one consent, and prints the list of servers for the user to install themselves if they want to keep them. It asks once to re-pin each design: claude-design pin to another design tool, claude-code (the default) first, then lovable and stitch, and removes the old adapter skills and the claude-design server
decisions.rejected: A doctor remedy only, with no format bump; a silent drop in setup

decisions.decision: The config_format 25 step, which asks about context7 and moves notion into addons:
decisions.ruling: Step 25 no longer asks the context7 question and no longer adds context7 or notion to addons:. A repo at 24 is never asked about a tool that step 26 then removes. Step 26 handles repos already at 25
decisions.rejected: Leave step 25 as it is

decisions.decision: A declined step 26
decisions.ruling: Amended by D26: each accepted part of the step 26 repo part is applied and stays; a declined part writes nothing; the stamp stays at 25 until every part is applied; doctor reports drift; setup offers only the remaining parts on the next run
decisions.rejected: Apply part of the step

decisions.decision: The checker and user_mcp_servers:
decisions.ruling: A checker rule refuses a user_mcp_servers: key in any pack.yaml. The D28 stdio runner guard over pack entries (checkPackRunners and its tests with the stacks/addon/context7 fixture) is removed. checkManifestRunners becomes a refusal of any mcpServers key in every plugin manifest (vwf and stackgen plugin.json), because a plugin declares no MCP server (D3); its runner helpers go, with a test that a plugin.json with mcpServers is refused (rulings round 2, gap 2)
decisions.rejected: Keep the runner guard for generated packs

decisions.decision: TOOL_TOKENS and the design-MCP guard
decisions.ruling: The guard becomes general: any mcp__plugin_vwf-tools_, mcp__plugin_design-tools_ or mcp__<name>__ server prefix in vwf prose is a finding, because vwf reaches no server, whoever installed it. claude-design stays in TOOL_TOKENS as a retired token with a comment that names the 2026-12-14 sunset of standalone Claude Design. The prescription tests keep their sample token; the guard tests change to the general prefix. The ENUMERATION_PEERS comment names claude-code, lovable and stitch as the design values
decisions.rejected: Remove the token and the guard; remove the token and keep a token-matched guard

decisions.decision: Commit order inside wave 1
decisions.ruling: The orchestrator commits the wave 1 units in the order U1, U2, U4, U3. U4 adds a rule that refuses user_mcp_servers:, and pre-commit stashes the unstaged edits of the units not yet committed, so a U4 commit before U1 would scan the three packs U1 deletes and fail the hook. U3 commits after U4, so its claude-design mentions beside claude-code pass with the new ENUMERATION_PEERS entry (rulings round 4, gap 1)

decisions.decision: Which stackgen call removes MCP keys for step 26 (rulings gap 1)
decisions.ruling: Extend remove:. It accepts any materialized slug, not only axis addon (stack-template SKILL.md:96-97 loses that refusal). Plain remove: <slug> deletes the component with all its keys. The form remove: <slug> mcp-only keeps the component and deletes only its MCP server keys from the vwf-tools manifest, claims.json and the lockfile local_plugin MCP records, and returns the removed server names. Step 26 calls plain remove: for context7, notion and the re-pinned claude-design, and remove: <slug> mcp-only for every other slug whose lockfile entry has an MCP key
decisions.rejected: A new verb retire-mcp:; plain remove: only, with a hand step for generated packs

decisions.decision: MCP keys on a machine whose repo is already at 26 (rulings gap 2)
decisions.ruling: Step 26 has two parts. The repo part (addons:, the claude-design re-pin) is the format step and runs once. The machine part runs on every /vwf:setup run, beside reconcile-claims: when this machine vwf-tools manifest holds any MCP server key, setup offers to remove them with one consent, through remove: <slug> mcp-only for each slug that claims one (and a plain key removal for a key no slug claims), and lists the servers for the user to install by hand. Declined: nothing is written and it is offered again next run. Doctor remedy /vwf:setup then points at this check
decisions.rejected: Run once in step 26, and a hand remedy in doctor for other machines

decisions.rejected: Drop only this repo claims and keep a key while another repo claims it

decisions.decision: How doctor decides a declared MCP server is available (rulings gap 9)
decisions.ruling: Doctor runs claude mcp list and looks for the exact server name of each ## MCP servers line in its output, at any scope. The command health-checks (connects to) each approved server; doctor accepts that as its one side effect and says so in the row. A listed server counts as available even if its health check fails, and the row notes the failure. A name that is not listed is drift. When the claude CLI is not on PATH, the row reads not checked. Each ## MCP servers line tells the user to install the server under that exact name (amended in rulings round 2, gap 6)
decisions.rejected: The session tool list (mcp__<server>__ tools)
